# Way of the Veil

Most people see the Rift as a wound — a tear in reality that leaks violet-black corruption into the world. Monks of the Way of the Veil see it as a threshold. The Rift isn't just damage. It's a membrane. And with enough discipline, you can learn to see through it.

These monks meditate on the Rift itself — not to resist it, but to attune to it. Their ki isn't life force. It's resonance. When they match the Rift's frequency exactly, the Veil parts. Distance becomes an illusion. Walls become suggestions. The space between here and there is just a matter of perception.

## Step Through the Veil

*3rd-level Way of the Veil feature*

You can slip through the Veil and emerge elsewhere. As an action, spend 1 ki point to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. You pass through the space between — and if that space is occupied, the Veil does not accommodate.

If your path crosses through any creature's space, that creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes Rift damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die + your Wisdom modifier, torn by the Veil's edge as you pass. On a success, it takes half damage.

You choose your destination. The Veil decides what's in the way.

## Veil Sight

*6th-level Way of the Veil feature*

Your daily meditation at the Veil's edge has sharpened your perception. You can spend 1 ki point to cast *See Invisibility* without material components. The Veil reveals what the material plane hides — you see through illusions, invisibility, and the tricks of creatures who think themselves unseen.

## Pull Through

*11th-level Way of the Veil feature*

You've learned to share what you see — whether the recipient is ready or not. As an action, spend 2 ki points and touch a creature. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be pulled partially into the Veil.

While pulled through, the creature experiences a full psychedelic trip — fractured perception, glimpses of realities that exist between moments, the overwhelming sensation that distance and time are lies. It is incapacitated until the end of your next turn. When it returns, the disorientation lingers — it has disadvantage on its first attack roll before the end of its next turn.

You've shown them the Veil. Whether they thank you for it is another matter.

## Walk Between

*17th-level Way of the Veil feature*

You no longer step through the Veil — you walk inside it. Once per long rest, you can spend 4 ki points to step fully into the space between realities for 1 minute.

While between, you are invisible, intangible, and immune to all damage. You can move through solid objects and creatures as if they weren't there. You can see and hear the material plane as though looking through frosted glass — clear enough to navigate, veiled enough to remind you that you're not quite there.

You cannot attack, cast spells, or affect creatures in any way while between. You are an observer, a ghost, a consciousness adrift in the Veil. You can end the state early as a bonus action, stepping back into reality at any point you can see.

To those watching, you simply cease to exist — and then, moments later, return from nowhere.
